before.title: Hypothesis and convention boundaries for the variational prerequisites
before.statement:
Two exact boundary checks. (i) Stationarity is first order. On $\mathbb R^2$ the polynomial $S(x,y)=x^2-y^2$ has differential $0$ at $(0,0)$, while $S(\varepsilon,0)=\varepsilon^2>0$ and $S(0,\varepsilon)=-\varepsilon^2<0$ for every $\varepsilon
e0$; a point where the first variation vanishes need not be a minimum. Consequently the equivalence of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] between stationarity and the coefficient equation, and the conversion by [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] of a vanishing first variation into pointwise equations, are first-order conditions: they carry no minimality and no existence content, and the example involves no adopted physical action. u:=\eta_{
u\mu}A^\mu$, $F_{\mu
u}:=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, $F^{\mu
u}:=\eta^{\mu\alpha}\eta^{
u eta}F_{\alpha eta}$, and $J^
u A_
u$ is the indicated contraction of the components of $J$ with the covector $A_
u$. Put $L:=- rac{1}{4\kappa}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+J^
u A_
u$ and $S[A]:=\int_U L\,d\lambda$, the $4$-dimensional Lebesgue integral of $L$ over $U$. Then $S[A]$ is a finite real number, and for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;V)$, with $h_
u:=\eta_{
u\mu}h^\mu$ and $G_{\mu
u}:=\partial_\mu h_
u-\partial_
u h_\mu$: (a) the map $s\mapsto S[A+sh]$ is the quadratic polynomial $S[A]+s\int_U\ell_1\,d\lambda+s^2\int_U\ell_2\,d\lambda$, where $\ell_1:=-\kappa^{-1}F^{\mu
u}\partial_\mu h_
u+J^
u h_
u$ and $\ell_2:=- rac{1}{4\kappa}G_{\mu
u}G^{\mu
u}$, so that its derivative at $s=0$ is $\int_U igl(-\kappa^{-1}F^{\mu
u}\partial_\mu h_
u+J^
u h_
u igr)d\lambda$; (b) that first variation also equals $\int_U igl(\kappa^{-1}\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}+J^
u igr)h_
u\,d\lambda$; (c) $A$ is stationary for $S$, meaning that the derivative in (a) vanishes for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;V)$, if and only if $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\kappa J^
u$ for every $
u$ on $U$, all derivatives being classical partial derivatives of the smooth field $A$. u}(s)=F_{\mu
u}+sG_{\mu
u}$ by linearity of the partial derivatives in the variation. Bilinearity of $\eta$ gives $F_{\mu
u}(s)F^{\mu
u}(s)=F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+2sF^{\mu
u}G_{\mu
u}+s^2G_{\mu
u}G^{\mu
u}$; the split $G_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu h_
u-\partial_
u h_\mu$ and the antisymmetry $F^{\mu
u}=-F^{
u\mu}$ give $F^{\mu
u}G_{\mu
u}=2F^{\mu
u}\partial_\mu h_
u$ (the two terms are equal after relabelling). Hence $L(A+sh)=L(A)+s\ell_1+s^2\ell_2$ pointwise on $N$ with the displayed $\ell_1,\ell_2$. The functions $L(A),\ell_1,\ell_2$ are continuous on the compact set $\overline U$, hence bounded, and the bounded open $U$ lies in a box of finite Lebesgue measure, so all three are integrable on $U$; linearity of the integral in $s$ gives the polynomial identity in (a) and, by differentiating the polynomial, the displayed derivative, with no exchange of limit and integral. Conversion. Fix $
u$. The function $x\mapsto F^{\mu
u}(x)$ (sum over $\mu$, with the repeated-index convention) is of class $C^1$ on the open set $U$, so by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]] its classical partial derivative $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}$ is its weak derivative; the test identity of [[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]] with the test function $h_
u\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ gives $\int_U F^{\mu
u}\partial_\mu h_
u\,d\lambda=-\int_U(\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u})h_
u\,d\lambda$. Substituting this into (a) yields (b). No boundary term remains precisely because $h$ is compactly supported in $U$; for a non-compactly-supported variation the identity fails, as the B example records. Coefficient equation. Put $g_
u:=\kappa^{-1}\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}+J^
u$, a continuous function on $U$; by (b) the first variation of $S$ at $A$ in direction $h$ is $\int_U\langle g,hangle\,d\lambda$. before.title: Fixed-endpoint variation of the relativistic particle functional
before.statement: Let $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ be an oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]) with $c>0$ the model's conversion constant, let $[a,b]$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, let $X:[a,b]\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve ([[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]), and let $A_\mu$ be a $C^2$ covector field on a neighbourhood of the image of $X$. For fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations $h:[a,b]\to V$ with $h(a)=h(b)=0$ and for $m,c>0$ and real $q$ consider $$S[X]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds .$$ Then for each such $h$ the curve $X+\varepsilon h$ remains future timelike for all sufficiently small $|\varepsilon|$, and stationarity of $S$ under all such variations is equivalent to $$m\frac{dU_\nu}{d\tau}=qF_{\nu\mu}U^\mu,\qquad \frac{d\tau}{ds}=\frac{\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}}c,\qquad F=dA,$$ where $U$ is the four-velocity and $\tau$ the proper-time parameter supplied by the observer-decomposition theorem ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]). This is a calculation about the chosen functional; adopting it as a physical particle action is an additional model assumption, and it makes no existence claim for coupled singular particles and fields.
before.strategy:
On the compact interval the strict inequalities of future timelikeness have positive margins, so $X+\varepsilon h$ remains future timelike for small $|\varepsilon|$ and the integrand is smooth on a compact parameter set; differentiation in $\varepsilon$ under the integral sign is justified by compactness. The free variation gives $\int mc\,\eta(\dot X,\dot h)/\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds=\int mU_
u\dot h^
u ds=-\int m(dU_
u/ds)h^
u ds$ after integration by parts, with the endpoint terms vanishing by $h(a)=h(b)=0$. The coupling variation is $q\int[(\partial_
u A_\mu)h^
u\dot X^\mu+A_
u\dot h^
u]ds=q\int(\partial_
u A_\mu-\partial_\mu A_
u)\dot X^\mu h^
u ds$ with the endpoint terms again zero, i.e. $q\int F_{
u\mu}\dot X^\mu h^
u ds$ for $F=dA$. Thus $\delta S=\int[-m\,dU_
u/ds+qF_{
u\mu}\dot X^\mu]h^
u ds$, and the fundamental variation lemma applied componentwise ([[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]]) makes every coefficient vanish (and conversely). Dividing by the strictly positive $d	au/ds$ obtained from the observer-decomposition theorem ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]], [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]) gives the stated equation; raising the index gives the tensor form. All objects are the affine-Minkowski ones of the SR supplier ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]).

All integrals in this particle lemma are finite-interval Riemann integrals. On $[a,b]$, $C^2$ means continuous components and continuous first and second derivatives with their one-sided endpoint values; equations at endpoints use those same one-sided derivatives. For fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variations $h:[a,b]\to V$ with $h(a)=h(b)=0$ and for $m,c>0$ and real $q$ consider $$S[X]=-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds .$$ Then for each such $h$ the curve $X+\varepsilon h$ remains future timelike for all sufficiently small $|\varepsilon|$, and stationarity of $S$ under all such variations is equivalent to $$m\frac{dU_\nu}{d\tau}=qF_{\nu\mu}U^\mu,\qquad \frac{d\tau}{ds}=\frac{\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}}c,\qquad F=dA,$$ where $U$ is the four-velocity and $\tau$ the proper-time parameter supplied by the observer-decomposition theorem ([[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]). This is a calculation about the chosen functional; adopting it as a physical particle action is an additional model assumption, and it makes no existence claim for coupled singular particles and fields. The coefficient-localization proof below is one-dimensional and choice-free; it does not invoke an AC-qualified Lebesgue fundamental lemma.
after.strategy:
Fix an inertial coordinate frame. The continuous functions $-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)$ and $\dot X^0$ have strictly positive minima on the compact nondegenerate interval; $h,\dot h$ are bounded there ([[thm-extreme-value-metric]]). Continuity of the quadratic form therefore keeps both margins positive for sufficiently small signed $\varepsilon$. The compact image of $X$ also has a finite neighbourhood cover inside the given potential domain; by shrinking $|\varepsilon|$ and using bounded $h$, every $X+\varepsilon h$ remains in that domain. Thus each admitted perturbation remains a future timelike curve with the same endpoints. The square-root derivative is the positive-base power derivative [[thm-real-power-continuity-and-derivatives]], with its agreement with the positive rational square root supplied by [[thm-real-power-agrees-with-rational-exponent]]. The two integrands and their $\varepsilon$ derivatives are continuous on one compact parameter rectangle, with the square-root argument bounded away from zero. Apply exactly the finite-interval Riemann theorem [[thm-differentiation-under-the-integral-sign-on-a-compact-rectangle]]; no Lebesgue conversion or AC-qualified parameter theorem is used.

The product and chain rules give
$$\delta S=\int_a^b mU_
u\dot h^
u ds+q\int_a^b[(\partial_
u A_\mu)(X)h^
u\dot X^\mu+A_
u(X)\dot h^
u]ds.$$
Here $	au'=\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}/c>0$ and $U=\dot X/	au'$ by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. All factors in the integrations by parts are $C^1$ on the closed interval, with continuous integrable derivatives. [[thm-integration-by-parts]], or the product rule followed by [[thm-ftc-second-part]], gives zero endpoint terms because $h(a)=h(b)=0$. Hence
$$\delta S=\int_a^b C_
u(s)h^
u(s)ds,\qquad C_
u=-m rac{dU_
u}{ds}+qF_{
u\mu}(X)\dot X^\mu.$$
Each coefficient is continuous on $[a,b]$.

For completeness prove the exact coefficient implication without the AC-qualified field lemma. If $C_
u(s_0)
e0$ at an interior point, choose its sign $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}$ and a small open interval $J\Subset(a,b)$ on which $\sigma C_
u\ge d>0$. Choose a nondegenerate closed subinterval $K\Subset J$. The ZF cutoff [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]], used in dimension one, supplies $\zeta\in C_c^\infty(J)$, $0\le\zeta\le1$, equal to one near $K$. Set the single nonzero variation component to $h^
u=\sigma\zeta$. This is an admitted fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variation, and Riemann monotonicity/additivity ([[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]], [[thm-additivity-over-subintervals]]) gives $\delta S=\int\sigma C_
u\zeta\ge d\,\mathrm{length}(K)>0$, contradicting stationarity. Thus all coefficients vanish on $(a,b)$ and, by their continuity, at both endpoints. Conversely their vanishing makes the first variation zero for every fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variation, not only the compact tests.

Divide by the positive $	au'$ to obtain $m\,dU_
u/d	au=qF_{
u\mu}U^\mu$. Raising the index with the constant metric gives the same vector equation. The relative endpoint and parameter conventions above retain the closed-interval branch. Existence of trajectories is not asserted. Only finite choices, finite-interval Riemann calculus and the explicitly ZF cutoff are used; no AC or Countable Choice is spent.

before.title: Compact gauge variation is boundary-free for conserved source
before.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), inherited through the componentwise fundamental-variation step of [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] and through [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]. Let $U,N,A,j,F,S$ and the constants $c,\mu_0,\varepsilon_0$ be as in clauses (a)-(b) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]]: $U\subseteq I	imes\Omega$ bounded open with $\overline U$ compact in $I	imes\Omega$, $N$ an open neighbourhood of $\overline U$, $A$ and $j$ smooth on $N$, $F_{\mu
u}=\partial_\mu A_
u-\partial_
u A_\mu$, $j=(cho,J)$ with the source fields of [[def-em-sources]], and $S[A]=c^{-1}\int_U igl[-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu
u}F^{\mu
u}+j^
u A_
u igr]d\lambda$. For $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ write $\partial\chi$ for the vector field with components $\partial_\mu\chi$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), a compactly supported smooth field variation, and let $A+\partial\chi$ denote componentwise addition.

(a) [Exact gauge difference, no boundary term] For every such $\chi$ one has $F_{\mu
u}(A+\partial\chi)=F_{\mu
u}(A)$ on $U$, because $\partial_\mu\partial_
u\chi-\partial_
u\partial_\mu\chi=0$ for the smooth $\chi$ ([[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]); consequently the field term of $S$ is unchanged and
$$S[A+\partial\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\,\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda=-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\,\chi\,d\lambda,$$
the second equality being the distributional integration-by-parts identity for the locally integrable fields $j^\mu$ and the smooth compactly supported $\chi$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]], [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]); no boundary term arises precisely because $\chi$ is compactly supported in $U$.

(b) [Equivalence for smooth sources] If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ on $U$ (the source is conserved), then $S[A+\partial\chi]=S[A]$ for every $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$. Conversely, if $S[A+\partial\chi]=S[A]$ for every such $\chi$, then $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ pointwise on $U$: the function $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is continuous on the open $U$ and pairs to zero against every compactly supported smooth $\chi$, so [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]] applies. Hence for smooth prescribed sources the invariance of the field action under all compact gauge variations is equivalent to the conservation of the four-current.

(c) [Maxwell-compatible sources] Suppose in addition that the field pair $(E,B)$ represented by $A$ through the potential dictionary of clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and the source fields $(ho,J)$ satisfy the smooth branch of the vacuum Maxwell equations on $U$ (equivalently, by clause (a) of [[pthm-em-tensor-maxwell-equivalence]], the tensor system $\partial_\mu F^{\mu
u}=-\mu_0j^
u$ together with the cyclic identity). Then clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives $\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ on $U$ ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]), which in the chart reads $\partial_\mu j^\mu=\partial_0(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=c^{-1}\partial_t(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=0$; hence $S[A+\partial\chi]=S[A]$ for every compact gauge variation.

(d) [Distributional reading] If $j^\mu$ is a distribution on $U$ ([[def-distributional-derivative]]), the gauge-difference pairing $c^{-1}\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chiangle$ is defined for every test function $\chi\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R)$ and equals $-c^{-1}\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chiangle$ by the signed definition of the distributional derivative; hence the pairing vanishes for every compact gauge variation if and only if $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ as a distribution. This is a statement about the pairing only: the smooth $j$ of the definition is retained whenever the functional $S$ itself is used, and no products of distributions are formed.

Scope: the item computes the gauge variation of the field action and its compatibility with source conservation; it does not derive the field equations from gauge invariance, does not assert that conservation of a source implies stationarity, does not treat global or topological obstructions, and uses no Noether machinery.
before.strategy:
Direct finite computation plus the fundamental lemma. (a) Since $A$ and $\chi$ are smooth, $F_{\mu
u}(A+\partial\chi)=F_{\mu
u}(A)+\partial_\mu\partial_
u\chi-\partial_
u\partial_\mu\chi=F_{\mu
u}(A)$ by [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]]; the quadratic field term is therefore constant along the gauge path, and only the source term changes: $S[A+\partial\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda$, using the linearity of the Lebesgue integral for the finite integrable functions ([[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]], [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]). Treat each $j^\mu$ as its regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]); the definition of the distributional derivative gives $\langle j^\mu,\partial_\mu\chiangle=-\langle\partial_\mu j^\mu,\chiangle$, and for the $C^1$ field $j^\mu$ the distributional derivative equals the classical one ([[thm-distributional-differentiation-is-continuous-and-commutes]]), which yields the displayed second equality. Because $\chi$ is compactly supported in the open $U$ there is no boundary term. (b) If $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ identically, (a) gives invariance. Conversely $\partial_\mu j^\mu$ is continuous on $U$, and the vanishing of its integral against every compactly supported smooth $\chi$ forces it to vanish pointwise by [[lem-em-fundamental-variation-lemma]]. (c) Under the smooth Maxwell branch, clause (a) of [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]] gives the continuity equation; the chart identity $\partial_\mu j^\mu=c^{-1}\partial_t(cho)+\operatorname{div}J=\partial_tho+\operatorname{div}J$ is the component computation of [[def-em-sources]] (c) and [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], so (b) applies. (d) For a distributional $j^\mu$ the pairing identity is the definition of the distributional derivative, and the vanishing criterion is the definition of the zero distribution. The Countable Choice assumption enters exactly through the two cited conversions (the pointwise localization against all smooth tests and the classical-compatibility of the distributional derivative); no other choice principle is used.

Excluded: derivation of the field equations from gauge invariance, stationarity conclusions, global or topological obstructions, Noether machinery, and rough-source products.

before.title: Relativistic prescribed-field particle action yields the Lorentz force
before.statement:
Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, [[def-countable-choice]]), needed only for the componentwise fundamental-variation step of the cited curve lemma. Let worldlines, four-velocities and proper times be those of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form with the component and potential dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and let $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$ be the framework's external rest-mass and charge parameters ([[def-em-sources]] (a)). Let $[a,b]$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, let $X:[a,b]\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline (clause (a) of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]), let $A_\mu$ be a $C^2$ covector field - the prescribed external four-potential - on a neighbourhood of the image of $X$, and let $S_{\rm pt}$ be the particle functional of clause (c) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]], i.e. the functional $-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds$ of [[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]].

Then, under the adopted stationary-action model for the particle sector ([[post-em-stationary-action-model]] (ii)), for every fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variation $h$ with $h(a)=h(b)=0$ the curve $X+\varepsilon h$ is future timelike for all sufficiently small $|\varepsilon|$, and the following are equivalent: (i) $X$ is stationary for $S_{\rm pt}$ under all such variations; (ii) $m\,dU_\nu/d\tau=qF_{\nu\mu}U^\mu$ on $[a,b]$, where $F=dA$ and $\tau$ is the proper time of $X$; (iii) the four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$ of the framework's adopted covariant coupling [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]], where $\Phi$ is the raised-index field operator $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$. In particular the stationary-action formulation of the particle sector is equivalent, for prescribed external potentials, to the adopted Lorentz coupling; the coordinate equations $\frac{dp}{dt}=q(E+v\times B)$ and $\frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$ of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] then hold wherever the laboratory reading is $C^2$.

Scope: the potential, hence the field, is prescribed and external to the particle; the particle's own field, radiation reaction and self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles, zero or variable mass, coupled particle-field existence and any approximation of the trajectory over a time interval. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.

before.title: Stationary functional need not be a minimum
before.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the cited suppliers; no additional choice is used. Work in the field-action setting of clauses (a)-(b) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with the square region $U:=(-1,1)^4$ and constants $c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]).

(a) [Source-free functional and rescaling] For $j\equiv0$, using the identity $\tfrac12F_{\mu\nu}F^{\mu\nu}=|B|^2-|E|^2/c^2$ of clause (b) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and $d\lambda=c\,dt\,d^3x$, the functional takes the physical form $S[A]=\int_U\bigl(\varepsilon_0|E|^2-|B|^2/\mu_0\bigr)/2\,dt\,d^3x$; it is homogeneous of degree two, $S[\lambda A]=\lambda^2S[A]$ for every real $\lambda$, because $F(\lambda A)=\lambda F(A)$.

(b) [A stationary configuration] $A=0$ is stationary for $S$ when $j\equiv0$: its first variation vanishes for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ because the first-variation integrand $-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu$ of clause (a) of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] contains the factor $F(A)=0$, and the source term vanishes with $j=0$.

(c) [Positive-action direction] For any $\theta\in C_c^\infty(U)$ with $\nabla\theta\not\equiv0$ take the variation $h$ with $h_0=\theta$ and $h_1=h_2=h_3=0$. Then $F_{0i}(h)=-\partial_i\theta$, so the represented field (clause (c) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]) is $E=c\,\nabla\theta$ and $B=0$, and
$$S[h]=c^{-1}\int_U\frac{1}{2\mu_0}\frac{|E|^2}{c^2}\,d\lambda=\frac{\varepsilon_0c^2}{2}\int_U|\nabla\theta|^2\,dt\,d^3x>0 .$$

(d) [Negative-action direction] Fix nonzero nonnegative bumps $\eta\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))$ and $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1)^3)$ with $\psi=1$ on the box $[1/2,1]\times[-1/4,1/4]^2$ and $|\eta|\ge\delta^\prime>0$ on a nondegenerate time subinterval $I_0\subseteq(-1,1)$ ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]), and for $N\in\mathbb N$ take the variation $h^{(N)}$ with $h^{(N)}_2(x)=\eta(x^0)\psi(x^1,x^2,x^3)(x^1)^N$ and all other components zero. Then $E_2=-c\,\eta^\prime(x^0)\psi\,(x^1)^N$ stays bounded, $|E|\le c\|\eta^\prime\|_\infty\|\psi\|_\infty$, while $B_3=\partial_1h^{(N)}_2=\eta\bigl(\partial_1\psi\,(x^1)^N+N\psi\,(x^1)^{N-1}\bigr)$; on the subbox $[1/2,1]\times[-1/4,1/4]^2\times I_0$ one has $\psi=1$ and $\partial_1\psi=0$, so $B_3=N\eta\,(x^1)^{N-1}$ there and, by the power rule, the product rule and the fundamental theorem ([[lem-derivative-of-a-power]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-chain-rule]], [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]]),
$$\int_U|B|^2\,dt\,d^3x\ \ge\ (\delta^\prime)^2N^2\int_{1/2}^1(x^1)^{2N-2}dx^1\cdot\tfrac14\cdot|I_0|=(\delta^\prime)^2N^2\,\frac{1-(1/2)^{2N-1}}{2N-1}\,\frac{|I_0|}{4}\ \ge\ c_1N,$$
for $N\ge1$, because $(1/2)^{2N-1}\le1/2$ by monotonicity of powers ([[lem-power-monotone]], [[lem-power-laws]]); hence $\int_U|B|^2\,dt\,d^3x\to\infty$ as $N\to\infty$. With the electric term bounded uniformly in $N$ ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]), $S[h^{(N)}]<0$ for all sufficiently large $N$. after.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the field-action measure suppliers ([[def-countable-choice]]); no additional choice is used. (a) [Coordinate and physical forms] With $x^0=ct$, set $U_t:=\{(t,x):(ct,x)\in U\}=(-1/c,1/c)\times(-1,1)^3$. The exact field dictionary gives
$$S[A]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\int_U(|E|^2/c^2-|B|^2)d\lambda=\frac12\int_{U_t}(\varepsilon_0|E|^2-|B|^2/\mu_0)dt\,d^3x.$$
Also $S[\lambda A]=\lambda^2S[A]$ for every real $\lambda$.

(b) [Stationarity] $A=0$ is stationary: the actual first-variation coefficient of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] is $-\mu_0^{-1}F^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu$, and the action variation is $c^{-1}$ times its integral. Both terms vanish at $F=0,j=0$.

(c) [Positive direction] Choose $\theta\in C_c^\infty(U)$ with $\nabla_x\theta\not\equiv0$. Set the covariant components $h_0=\theta,h_i=0$, equivalently the contravariant variation $h^0=-\theta,h^i=0$. Then $E=c\nabla_x\theta$, $B=0$, and
$$S[h]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\int_U|\nabla_x\theta|^2d\lambda>0.$$

(d) [Negative directions with a fixed compact support] Choose nonzero nonnegative smooth bumps $\eta,\varphi,\psi_2,\psi_3\in C_c^\infty((-1/2,1/2))$ using [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Extend them by zero to $\mathbb R$. For integers $N\ge1$ define the contravariant variation with only its second spatial component nonzero:
$$h^{(N)2}(x)=\eta(x^0)\varphi(Nx^1)\psi_2(x^2)\psi_3(x^3).$$
All supports lie in one fixed compact subset of $U$. Writing $f_N=h^{(N)2}$, its fields are $E=-c(\partial_0f_N)e_2$ and $B=-(\partial_3f_N)e_1+(\partial_1f_N)e_3$. Define finite constants, with all one-dimensional integrals over $(-1,1)$,
$$C_E=(\int\eta'^2)(\int\varphi^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3^2),\quad C_B=(\int\eta^2)(\int\varphi'^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3^2)>0,$$
$$C_3=(\int\eta^2)(\int\varphi^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3'^2)\ge0.$$
Exact substitution and Fubini give
$$\int_U|E|^2/c^2d\lambda=C_E/N,\qquad\int_U|B|^2d\lambda=C_BN+C_3/N,$$

For nonzero $\lambda$, their rescalings keep their respective signs, and each action tends to zero in absolute value as $\lambda\to0$. A single fixed negative direction is not claimed to change sign under rescaling.

(e) [Every usual neighbourhood] Fix those two directions before rescaling. For each derivative multi-index, every compact-set supremum of a derivative of $\lambda h_\pm$ is $|\lambda|$ times the finite supremum for that fixed smooth compactly supported direction. Thus both tend to zero in the usual $C^k$, smooth compact-convergence and fixed-support and LF test-function topologies ([[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]], [[def-test-function-topology]]) (and in any usual function-space topology with continuous scalar multiplication). before.title: A compact test variation and gauge-source sign check
before.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the cited theorems. Work in the field-action setting of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with $U=(-1,1)^4$, constants $c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), and the component dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]: $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{10}=-E_1/c$.

(a) [Source-free zero field] For $j\equiv0$ and $A=0$ the first-variation integrand $-(4\mu_0)^{-1}F_{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu$ of clause (a) of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] vanishes identically for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, because $F(A)=0$ and $j=0$; hence every compact first variation of $S$ at $A=0$ is zero and $A=0$ is stationary.

(b) [A non-trivial compact test variation] Let $A$ be the smooth potential with $A_0(x)=x^1$ and $A_1=A_2=A_3=0$, and let $j\equiv0$. Then $F_{01}=-\partial_1A_0=-1$, $F^{01}=+1$, $F^{10}=-1$ and all other components vanish, so the represented field is $E=(c,0,0)$, $B=0$ (clause (b) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]) and $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=0$ on $U$. By the equivalence of [[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]], $A$ is stationary; directly, for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ the first variation of $S$ at $A$ is
$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=-\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_0h_1-\partial_1h_0\bigr)d\lambda=\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_1h_0-\partial_0h_1\bigr)d\lambda=0,$$
where each of $\int_U\partial_0h_1\,d\lambda$ and $\int_U\partial_1h_0\,d\lambda$ vanishes by the fundamental theorem in one variable combined with Fubini, and no boundary term appears because $h$ is compactly supported in $U$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]).

(c) [Gauge-source sign check] Now let $j$ be the smooth source with $j^0=c\rho(x^0)$, $j^1=j^2=j^3=0$, where $\rho\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))$, $\rho\ge0$, $\rho\not\equiv0$, so $\partial_\mu j^\mu=c\rho'(x^0)$ ([[def-em-sources]]). $$S[A+\partial\chi]-S[A]=c^{-1}\int_Uj^\mu\partial_\mu\chi\,d\lambda=\Bigl(\int_{-1}^1\rho\varphi'\,dx^0\Bigr)\Bigl(\int_{(-1,1)^3}\psi\,d^3x\Bigr)=-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\chi\,d\lambda .$$

If instead $\rho\equiv\rho_0$ is constant (a conserved static source), then $\partial_\mu j^\mu=0$ and the difference vanishes for every compact gauge, in agreement with the conservation criterion of [[pthm-em-action-gauge-source-compatibility]].

(d) [Scope] The example is an exact computation in the declared smooth finite-region model; it asserts no existence of sources or fields, no numerical value of $\mu_0$, and no global gauge statement.

batch39_all7_after.statement:
The model adopts the following formulation principle as an alternative to postulating the field equations and the force law directly. (i) [Field sector] A smooth field $A:N\to\mathbb R^4$ on the region $U$ of clause (a) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] is dynamically admissible exactly when it is stationary for the field action $S[A]$ under all compactly supported smooth variations $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ in the sense of clause (b) of that definition: $\frac{d}{ds}\big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=0$ for every such $h$. This is an adopted assumption of the model, not a theorem, not a derivation from the remaining postulates and not an empirical result. It asserts stationarity only: it does not assert that a stationary configuration is a local or global minimum, that stationary configurations exist or are unique, that the action functional is uniquely determined or forced by symmetry, that no other action formulation is possible, or that the two sectors can be coupled into a single well-posed action for singular sources. batch39_all7_after.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the cited theorems. Work in the field-action setting of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with $U=(-1,1)^4$, constants $c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), and the component dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]: $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{10}=-E_1/c$.

(a) [Source-free zero field] For $j\equiv0$ and $A=0$ the first-variation coefficient (whose integral is multiplied by $c^{-1}$) $-\mu_0^{-1}F^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu$ of clause (a) of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] vanishes identically for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, because $F(A)=0$ and $j=0$; hence every compact first variation of $S$ at $A=0$ is zero and $A=0$ is stationary.

(b) [A non-trivial compact test variation] Let $A$ be the smooth potential with $A_0(x)=x^1$ and $A_1=A_2=A_3=0$, and let $j\equiv0$. Then $F_{01}=-\partial_1A_0=-1$, $F^{01}=+1$, $F^{10}=-1$ and all other components vanish, so the represented field is $E=(c,0,0)$, $B=0$ (clause (b) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]) and $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=0$ on $U$. By the equivalence of [[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]], $A$ is stationary; directly, for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ the first variation of $S$ at $A$ is
$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=-\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_0h_1-\partial_1h_0\bigr)d\lambda=\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_1h_0-\partial_0h_1\bigr)d\lambda=0,$$
where each of $\int_U\partial_0h_1\,d\lambda$ and $\int_U\partial_1h_0\,d\lambda$ vanishes by the fundamental theorem in one variable combined with Fubini, and no boundary term appears because $h$ is compactly supported in $U$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]).

(c) [Gauge-source sign check with actual overlap] Independently choose the smooth prescribed source $j^0=c\rho(x^0)$, $j^i=0$, with nonzero nonnegative $\rho\in C_c^\infty((-1/4,1/4))$ extended by zero. Choose $0\le\zeta\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))$ with $\zeta=1$ near $[-1/2,1/2]$, and nonzero nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1)^3)$, supplied by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Put $\varphi_\pm(u)=(2\pm u)\zeta(u)$ and $\chi_\pm(x)=\varphi_\pm(x^0)\psi(x^1,x^2,x^3)$. Both $\varphi_\pm$ are nonnegative compact bumps, but they are not globally monotone: on the entire support of $\rho$ their derivatives equal $+1$ and $-1$, respectively. $$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi_\pm]-S[A]=\left(\int_{-1}^1\rho\varphi_\pm'\,dx^0\right)\left(\int_{(-1,1)^3}\psi\,d^3x\right)=\pm\left(\int\rho\right)\left(\int\psi\right),$$

Integration by parts gives exactly the same value as $-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\chi_\pm d\lambda$ with $\partial_\mu j^\mu=c\rho'$. This verifies the relative sign of the $+j^\mu A_\mu$ coupling, the raised-vector/covariant-lowered gauge shift and the conservation condition, using explicitly overlapping supports. If instead $\rho$ is constant on the whole neighbourhood, the source is conserved and every compact gauge difference is zero. No compact nonzero globally increasing or decreasing function is used.

(d) [Scope] The example is an exact computation in the declared smooth finite-region model; it asserts no existence of sources or fields, no numerical value of $\mu_0$, and no global gauge statement.

(a) [Coordinate and physical forms] With $x^0=ct$, set $U_t:=\{(t,x):(ct,x)\in U\}=(-1/c,1/c)\times(-1,1)^3$. The exact field dictionary gives
$$S[A]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\int_U(|E|^2/c^2-|B|^2)d\lambda=\frac12\int_{U_t}(\varepsilon_0|E|^2-|B|^2/\mu_0)dt\,d^3x.$$

(c) [Positive direction] Choose $\theta\in C_c^\infty(U)$ with $\nabla_x\theta\not\equiv0$. Set the covariant components $h_0=\theta,h_i=0$, equivalently the contravariant variation $h^0=-\theta,h^i=0$. Then $E=c\nabla_x\theta$, $B=0$, and
$$S[h]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\int_U|\nabla_x\theta|^2d\lambda>0.$$

(d) [Negative directions with a fixed compact support] Choose nonzero nonnegative smooth bumps $\eta,\varphi,\psi_2,\psi_3\in C_c^\infty((-1/2,1/2))$ using [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Extend them by zero to $\mathbb R$. For integers $N\ge1$ define the contravariant variation with only its second spatial component nonzero:
$$h^{(N)2}(x)=\eta(x^0)\varphi(Nx^1)\psi_2(x^2)\psi_3(x^3).$$
All supports lie in one fixed compact subset of $U$. Writing $f_N=h^{(N)2}$, its fields are $E=-c(\partial_0f_N)e_2$ and $B=-(\partial_3f_N)e_1+(\partial_1f_N)e_3$. Define finite constants, with all one-dimensional integrals over $(-1,1)$,
$$C_E=(\int\eta'^2)(\int\varphi^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3^2),\quad C_B=(\int\eta^2)(\int\varphi'^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3^2)>0,$$
$$C_3=(\int\eta^2)(\int\varphi^2)(\int\psi_2^2)(\int\psi_3'^2)\ge0.$$
Exact substitution and Fubini give
$$\int_U|E|^2/c^2d\lambda=C_E/N,\qquad\int_U|B|^2d\lambda=C_BN+C_3/N,$$
$$S[h^{(N)}]=\frac{1}{2c\mu_0}\left(\frac{C_E-C_3}{N}-C_BN\right)\longrightarrow-\infty.$$
Thus a fixed sufficiently large $N$ supplies one negative direction $h_-$; the direction $h_+$ of (c) is positive. For nonzero $\lambda$, their rescalings keep their respective signs, and each action tends to zero in absolute value as $\lambda\to0$. A single fixed negative direction is not claimed to change sign under rescaling.

(e) [Every usual neighbourhood] Fix those two directions before rescaling. For each derivative multi-index, every compact-set supremum of a derivative of $\lambda h_\pm$ is $|\lambda|$ times the finite supremum for that fixed smooth compactly supported direction. Thus both tend to zero in the usual $C^k$, smooth compact-convergence and fixed-support and LF test-function topologies ([[def-fixed-support-test-function-frechet-space]], [[def-test-function-topology]]) (and in any usual function-space topology with continuous scalar multiplication). Every such neighbourhood of zero therefore contains configurations of positive and negative action, arbitrarily small in magnitude. The stationary zero is neither a local minimum nor a local maximum. This is a computation in the declared smooth finite-region model, not a claim about actual fields or measurements; other sources or boundary/variation restrictions require their own analysis.

consumer_reviews.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, inherited from the cited theorems. Work in the field-action setting of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] with $U=(-1,1)^4$, constants $c,\mu_0>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ ([[def-em-si-conventions]]), and the component dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]: $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{10}=-E_1/c$.

(a) [Source-free zero field] For $j\equiv0$ and $A=0$ the first-variation coefficient (whose integral is multiplied by $c^{-1}$) $-\mu_0^{-1}F^{\mu\nu}\partial_\mu h_\nu+j^\nu h_\nu$ of clause (a) of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] vanishes identically for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$, because $F(A)=0$ and $j=0$; hence every compact first variation of $S$ at $A=0$ is zero and $A=0$ is stationary.

(b) [A non-trivial compact test variation] Let $A$ be the smooth potential with $A_0(x)=x^1$ and $A_1=A_2=A_3=0$, and let $j\equiv0$. Then $F_{01}=-\partial_1A_0=-1$, $F^{01}=+1$, $F^{10}=-1$ and all other components vanish, so the represented field is $E=(c,0,0)$, $B=0$ (clause (b) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]) and $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=0$ on $U$. By the equivalence of [[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]], $A$ is stationary; directly, for every $h\in C_c^\infty(U;\mathbb R^4)$ the first variation of $S$ at $A$ is
$$\frac{d}{ds}\Big|_{s=0}S[A+sh]=-\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_0h_1-\partial_1h_0\bigr)d\lambda=\frac{1}{c\mu_0}\int_U\bigl(\partial_1h_0-\partial_0h_1\bigr)d\lambda=0,$$
where each of $\int_U\partial_0h_1\,d\lambda$ and $\int_U\partial_1h_0\,d\lambda$ vanishes by the fundamental theorem in one variable combined with Fubini, and no boundary term appears because $h$ is compactly supported in $U$ ([[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]], [[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]], [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]]).

(c) [Gauge-source sign check with actual overlap] Independently choose the smooth prescribed source $j^0=c\rho(x^0)$, $j^i=0$, with nonzero nonnegative $\rho\in C_c^\infty((-1/4,1/4))$ extended by zero. Choose $0\le\zeta\in C_c^\infty((-1,1))$ with $\zeta=1$ near $[-1/2,1/2]$, and nonzero nonnegative $\psi\in C_c^\infty((-1,1)^3)$, supplied by [[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]. Put $\varphi_\pm(u)=(2\pm u)\zeta(u)$ and $\chi_\pm(x)=\varphi_\pm(x^0)\psi(x^1,x^2,x^3)$. Both $\varphi_\pm$ are nonnegative compact bumps, but they are not globally monotone: on the entire support of $\rho$ their derivatives equal $+1$ and $-1$, respectively. Use the contravariant gauge variations $(\partial^\sharp\chi_\pm)^\mu=\eta^{\mu\nu}\partial_\nu\chi_\pm$ from [[pthm-em-action-gauge-source-compatibility]]. Then
$$S[A+\partial^\sharp\chi_\pm]-S[A]=\left(\int_{-1}^1\rho\varphi_\pm'\,dx^0\right)\left(\int_{(-1,1)^3}\psi\,d^3x\right)=\pm\left(\int\rho\right)\left(\int\psi\right),$$
which is strictly positive for $+$ and strictly negative for $-$, since both factors are positive. Integration by parts gives exactly the same value as $-c^{-1}\int_U(\partial_\mu j^\mu)\chi_\pm d\lambda$ with $\partial_\mu j^\mu=c\rho'$. This verifies the relative sign of the $+j^\mu A_\mu$ coupling, the raised-vector/covariant-lowered gauge shift and the conservation condition, using explicitly overlapping supports. If instead $\rho$ is constant on the whole neighbourhood, the source is conserved and every compact gauge difference is zero. No compact nonzero globally increasing or decreasing function is used.

(d) [Scope] The example is an exact computation in the declared smooth finite-region model; it asserts no existence of sources or fields, no numerical value of $\mu_0$, and no global gauge statement.

(a) is the first-variation formula of [[lem-em-compact-field-variation]] with $F=0$ and $j=0$; the pointwise vanishing of the integrand gives a vanishing integral for every $h$. (b) The components follow from clause (a) of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]: $F_{01}=\partial_0A_1-\partial_1A_0=-1$, $F^{01}=\eta^{00}\eta^{11}F_{01}=+1$, $F^{10}=-1$. The coefficient equation $\partial_\mu F^{\mu\nu}=-\mu_0j^\nu$ holds because $F$ is constant and $j=0$, so [[pthm-em-action-maxwell-variation]] gives stationarity. The direct computation uses the first-variation expression of the cited lemma and the one-variable fundamental theorem for the compactly supported functions $h_0,h_1$, with Fubini reducing the four-dimensional integral; the absence of boundary terms is exactly the compact-support hypothesis. (c) Apply the corrected raised-gradient gauge formula. The cutoff $\zeta$ is one on a neighbourhood of the support of $\rho$, so $\zeta'=0$ there and $\varphi_+'=1$, $\varphi_-'=-1$ there. Although both compact functions must turn back to zero outside that plateau, those derivative changes do not meet $\rho$. Thus Fubini gives the two signed products of positive integrals exactly. The signs agree with one-dimensional [[thm-integration-by-parts]], whose endpoint term is zero because the factors are compactly supported. Constant $\rho$ instead gives $\int\rho\varphi_\pm'=0$ by FTC, consistently with source conservation. The finite-interval Riemann particle-sector calculation is choice-free: the field-sector Countable Choice convention of [[def-em-field-action-definition]] is not used here. Let worldlines, four-velocities and proper times be those of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]], let $F$ be the electromagnetic two-form with the component and potential dictionary of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and let $m>0$ and $q\in\mathbb R$ be the framework's external rest-mass and charge parameters ([[def-em-sources]] (a)). Let $[a,b]$ be a nondegenerate compact interval, let $X:[a,b]\to A$ be a $C^2$ future timelike massive worldline (clause (a) of [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]]), let $A_\mu$ be a $C^2$ covector field - the prescribed external four-potential - on a neighbourhood of the image of $X$, and let $S_{\rm pt}$ be the particle functional of clause (c) of [[def-em-field-action-definition]], i.e. the functional $-mc\int_a^b\sqrt{-\eta(\dot X,\dot X)}\,ds+q\int_a^bA_\mu(X)\dot X^\mu\,ds$ of [[lem-em-particle-curve-variation]].

Then, under the adopted stationary-action model for the particle sector ([[post-em-stationary-action-model]] (ii)), for every fixed-endpoint $C^2$ variation $h$ with $h(a)=h(b)=0$ the curve $X+\varepsilon h$ is future timelike for all sufficiently small $|\varepsilon|$, and the following are equivalent: (i) $X$ is stationary for $S_{\rm pt}$ under all such variations; (ii) $m\,dU_\nu/d\tau=qF_{\nu\mu}U^\mu$ on $[a,b]$, where $F=dA$ and $\tau$ is the proper time of $X$; (iii) the four-force equation $m\,dU/d\tau=q\,\Phi(U)$ of the framework's adopted covariant coupling [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]], where $\Phi$ is the raised-index field operator $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$. In particular the stationary-action formulation of the particle sector is equivalent, for prescribed external potentials, to the adopted Lorentz coupling; the coordinate equations $\frac{dp}{dt}=q(E+v\times B)$ and $\frac{d(\gamma mc^2)}{dt}=qE\cdot v$ of [[pthm-em-relativistic-lorentz-force]] then hold wherever the laboratory reading is $C^2$.

Scope: the potential, hence the field, is prescribed and external to the particle; the particle's own field, radiation reaction and self-force are excluded, as are magnetic monopoles, zero or variable mass, coupled particle-field existence and any approximation of the trajectory over a time interval. The equivalence is conditional on the adopted postulates and makes no empirical claim.
